purpose: A bounded method for running a live medical-alert monitoring subscription honestly over years: holding one authoritative account record whose address, access details, contact tree and equipment inventory are dated rather than assumed, proving the signal chain on a written test cadence tied to the monitoring platform's supervision window, reading device-health and supervisory events instead of asserting battery, range or response characteristics, keeping family and professional caregivers informed strictly inside the wearer's own disclosure permissions, restoring an account after every real activation and reconstructing the whole chain before explaining anything after a missed signal, reducing nuisance activations without quietly removing protection, migrating a fleet when a carrier or platform retires, ending accounts with dignity when a wearer moves to higher care or dies, proving the exit is no harder than the entry, reading the recurring book as a mechanism traced to the operator's own invoices, and earning referrals only at moments that demonstrated competence rather than at moments of grief.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the business resells monitoring capacity bought from a monitoring centre under contract and maintains the wearer's equipment; it operates no clinical service and employs no licensed clinician in the service role
the wearer is the customer for the whole life of the subscription even when an adult child or another relative pays for it

reliability characteristics such as battery endurance, radio or cellular range, detection behaviour and monitoring-centre answering performance are properties of this account's specific equipment and the operator's specific monitoring contract, established by test and supervisory record rather than by brochure

alarm-monitoring licensing, automatic-renewal and cancellation-channel rules, false-alarm ordinances, personal-data handling duties and refund obligations differ by jurisdiction and change over time; every rule named here is an obligation class the operator must verify currently in their own jurisdiction

account economics are governed by the operator's own monitoring invoice, equipment costs and service records, so every figure is expressed as a mechanism the operator instantiates rather than as an industry number
exclusions: the buyer triangle, referral-channel building with discharge planners, home-care agencies and senior centres, transparent offer and price design, pre-sale vulnerable-consumer rules and honest competitive positioning — that is the market and ethical-senior-sales knowledge base this one receives accounts from

device-type selection between in-home and mobile units, honest framing of fall-detection class capabilities, home range and connectivity assessment, mounting, monitoring-centre integration, initial emergency-contact-tree construction, the mandatory installation-day end-to-end signal test and first wearer training — that is the device setup, monitoring integration and testing knowledge base

acquisition economics, channel spend allocation and the cost of winning a new account, which belong to the acquisition knowledge base; this knowledge base covers only what happens to an account once it is live

any clinical judgment or medical advice: fall-risk assessment, capacity or competence determination, medication questions, interpretation of what happened to a wearer during an event, or whether an older adult can safely live alone
personalized financial, legal, tax, estate or insurance advice, including probate questions after a wearer dies and whether any benefit programme reimburses a monitoring subscription

asserting specific prices, wholesale monitoring rates, margins, response times, battery endurance figures, tenure durations or churn percentages as fact; all money and performance content is a mechanism or a qualitative band the operator instantiates from their own contracts, invoices and test records
retention campaigns, save-desk scripting, win-back offers and any process whose purpose is to make leaving harder than joining

glossary.definition: A periodic automatic check-in a monitored unit sends to the monitoring centre to say it is still present, powered and reachable; its absence past the platform's supervision window is what lets a centre report a unit missing rather than silently assume it is fine.

The interval the monitoring platform allows between supervisory signals before it treats a unit as missing; it is the ceiling that a test cadence and a health routine must be designed under, and it is a property of the operator's own monitoring contract rather than a universal figure.

A deliberate end-to-end activation run on a schedule to prove that a press in the wearer's actual living space still reaches the monitoring centre, is identified to the right account, and establishes voice where the equipment supports it; the recorded result is the account's own evidence that the service worked.

The ordered list of people the monitoring centre attempts on an activation, with relationship, current number and the standing instruction for each; it decays continuously as contacts move, change numbers, become unavailable or die, which is why it is a maintained field rather than a stored one.

Any event that sends an alarm signal to the monitoring centre, whether from a button press, a detection-class feature, or accident; every activation leaves the account degraded in some way until it is deliberately restored.

An activation that did not correspond to a need for help — a pendant pressed by a chair arm, handling during a care transfer, a dropped unit read as a fall — costly in responder goodwill and family trust, and dangerous mainly because the cheapest fix is to make the device less likely to fire at all.

The contracted central station that receives signals, attempts voice contact, works the contact tree and requests public emergency services under the account's instructions; the operator resells its capacity and depends on its records, retention practices and platform behaviour, none of which the operator controls.

The signal path a unit depends on to reach the centre — a cellular generation, a broadband or voice service, or a fixed line — recorded per account because it is the field that determines who is affected when a carrier or service is retired.

A temporary hold on a live account, legitimate only when it genuinely serves the customer, such as a rehabilitation stay that may end with a return home; it becomes a retention device the moment it is offered to avoid recording a cancellation, so it carries an end date and an owner.

The recorded category of why an account ended — death of the wearer, move to higher care, hospitalisation, cost decision, non-wear, service failure, competitor, or an account the wearer never wanted — used to route the ending to the right handling path and to make the book readable; some classes are never treated as opportunities to save an account.

nodes.definition: State in one place what the monthly subscription actually buys, so that every later conversation — a routine test call, a furious call at two in the morning after an incident, a cancellation — is measured against the same promise instead of against whatever a frightened relative assumed. The promise in this business is narrow and mechanical: a press or a detected event produces a signal, the signal reaches the contracted monitoring centre, an operator attempts voice contact and works the emergency contact tree and public emergency services according to the account's standing instructions, and the business keeps the equipment and the account record in a condition where that chain can work. The refusals are equally explicit and equally written down: it is not a caregiver, not a nurse call, not a medical service, not a fall-prevention device, not a guarantee that help arrives in time, and not a substitute for anyone's clinical judgment. The charter also fixes the conduct limits that hold for the whole life of the subscription — never frighten a family into keeping a service, never make leaving harder than joining, never state a battery, range, detection or response characteristic that has not been verified on this account's own equipment. Every work unit downstream inherits these lines and may narrow them, never widen them.

included: the written promise of the live service and the signal chain it describes
the enumerated refusals, including every clinical refusal
the conduct limits that bind the business for the whole subscription life
excluded: the pre-sale offer, price disclosure and contract terms, which belong to the acquisition knowledge base
installation, device selection and the first end-to-end signal test, which belong to the setup knowledge base
any clinical or medical determination about the wearer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the monitoring contract, dispatch procedure or fleet transport changes, or a complaint shows staff acting on a promise the charter never made

pros.claim: A narrow written promise gives staff a defensible and honest answer at the exact moment emotion is highest
pros.example: a night call where a son demands to know why the pendant did not stop his mother falling, answered from the same promise the family was given at sale

pros.claim: Naming the refusals in advance stops sympathetic staff inventing obligations the business cannot keep
pros.example: a technician declining to say whether a wearer should still be using the stairs and pointing the family to their own clinician

cons.claim: A narrow promise reads as cold to a family in crisis who wanted reassurance rather than scope
cons.example: a daughter hearing the phrase about relaying signals twenty minutes after an ambulance left, and experiencing it as evasion

cons.claim: A charter written once drifts as the monitoring contract and the device fleet change underneath it
cons.example: a promise still describing a fixed-line call path years after the book moved mostly to cellular units

failure_modes: letting the promise expand informally through kind improvisation until the business is treated as a care service
producing the charter as a liability shield during a service-recovery conversation instead of as a statement of scope
never showing the charter to the customer again after the sale, so only the business knows what was promised
acceptance_tests: the charter states the signal chain, the enumerated refusals and the conduct limits on one page a customer can actually read
a sampled service conversation can be mapped to a promise or a refusal already in the charter without inventing a new one
revisit_triggers: the monitoring centre contract or its dispatch procedure changes
the device fleet changes class or transport
a complaint reveals a promise staff believed existed that the charter never made

nodes.definition: Maintain one authoritative record per live account that every routine, every alarm and every billing action reads from, and treat its currency as a service obligation rather than as administration. The record carries the wearer's legal name and the name they actually answer to, the service address with the details a responder needs — which door, unit number, gate or entry code, lockbox, stairs, a dog — the equipment inventory by serial and model or firmware revision, the transport each unit signals over, the monitoring centre's own account identifier, the ordered contact tree with relationships and current numbers, the standing instructions the wearer chose, the billing instrument and whose it is, the disclosure and authority permissions, and the dated history of tests, activations, visits and consumable replacements. Two properties make it worth the effort. It is reconciled against the copy the monitoring centre holds on a stated cadence rather than assumed identical, because a change made by phone to one copy and never to the other is the classic cause of a responder at the wrong door. And every field carries the date it was last confirmed, so staleness becomes visible work rather than an invisible risk. An account whose record has gone stale is not a healthy account even when every device on it is working perfectly.

included: the per-account field set including responder access details and transport
reconciliation against the monitoring centre's copy on a stated cadence
per-field last-confirmed dating that makes staleness visible
excluded: the initial capture of these fields during installation, which is the setup knowledge base's work
the choice of billing or customer-record software
clinical or diagnostic information about the wearer, which this business has no basis to hold

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reconciliation run finds drift between the two copies, or a real incident exposes a field the record does not carry

pros.claim: Dating every field converts silent decay into a schedulable work item
pros.example: a contact-tree entry last confirmed two winters ago surfacing on a review queue before an emergency finds it first

pros.claim: One reconciled record removes the argument about whose copy was right after an incident
pros.example: an address correction given verbally to the monitoring centre but never entered locally, caught by reconciliation instead of by a crew at the old address

cons.claim: Field-level confirmation work grows with the book and competes with revenue-producing work
cons.example: a growing account count where currency confirmations start to consume more hours than new installations

cons.claim: A rich record concentrates sensitive household information and raises the handling duty
cons.example: holding entry codes, key locations and dated event histories for many households in one system

failure_modes: keeping the real truth in a technician's phone or memory rather than in the account record
letting the local copy and the monitoring centre's copy drift with no reconciliation step at all
pruning the record down to billing and contact names because the responder-relevant fields are rarely read
acceptance_tests: a sampled account shows every responder-relevant field with a last-confirmed date and a matching value in the monitoring centre's copy
the field list demonstrably covers access details and transport, not only names, numbers and billing
revisit_triggers: the monitoring platform changes its data model, identifiers or export format
a responder reports being delayed by wrong or missing access details
personal-data handling obligations change in the operator's jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Decide, record and then honour two separate questions per account: who may be told what about the wearer, and who may change or end the service. They are not the same list, and collapsing them is the origin of most family friction in this business. While the wearer holds their own affairs, they are the primary authority over both; a paying adult child is a payer, which is not automatically a decision-maker and not automatically an information recipient. The map records, in the wearer's own stated preference, which people may be told that an activation occurred, which may be told what happened during it, which may add or remove contacts, which may change the service address, and which may cancel. It records whether a formal legal authority — a power of attorney, guardianship or equivalent instrument, whose form, scope and effect are an obligation class the operator must verify currently in their own jurisdiction — has been presented, what type it is and when it was checked. It records that the wearer may revise any of it at any time, and the date of their last statement. The business's job is to hold the line the wearer drew, including against a well-meaning relative holding the credit card.

included: the disclosure list and the separate authority list per account
capture of any presented legal-authority instrument by type and verification date, as an obligation class
the wearer's standing right to revise both lists
excluded: determining capacity or competence, which is a clinical and legal judgment this business never makes
interpreting or drafting a legal instrument, which is counsel's work
consent to the sales contract itself, which belongs to the acquisition knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a family dispute, a presented or revoked authority instrument, or a jurisdictional change in privacy or consumer-authority obligations

pros.claim: Separating payer from decision-maker prevents the most common dignity failure in a family-funded subscription
pros.example: a son who pays being told that an activation occurred but not his mother's account of what she was doing when she fell, exactly as she asked

pros.claim: A recorded map lets a night operator answer a stranger's call without improvising
pros.example: a caller claiming to be a nephew being given only the occurrence fact, because that is all the map lists him for

cons.claim: Honouring a restrictive map can look obstructive to a family acting in genuine good faith
cons.example: a niece who lives nearest being refused detail she believes she needs while she is already driving over

cons.claim: Legal-authority instruments vary widely and service staff are not qualified to judge their scope
cons.example: a document presented as a power of attorney that may or may not extend to service contracts, held pending the operator's own counsel

failure_modes: letting whoever pays the bill become the de facto decision-maker because they are easier to reach
accepting a verbal claim of authority over the telephone with no recorded basis
never re-asking the wearer after a divorce, a death in the family or a move changes who is around them
acceptance_tests: each live account carries a disclosure list and an authority list, each dated to the wearer's own statement
any presented legal-authority instrument is recorded with its type and the date it was checked against the operator's own policy or counsel
revisit_triggers: the wearer's household or family situation changes
a legal-authority instrument is presented, revoked or expires
privacy or consumer-authority obligations change in the operator's jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Run a standing programme of deliberate end-to-end test signals so that the chain from button to monitoring centre is proven to still work rather than assumed to. Four design decisions carry the programme. The interval, which must sit inside the supervision window the operator's platform enforces before it would report a unit missing, and must be short enough that a dead path is found within a period the operator is willing to defend to a family. Who initiates, since a wearer-initiated test doubles as practice at pressing the button when nothing is wrong, while an operator-initiated test costs the wearer no effort and reaches the people who would never call. What counts as a pass, which is a signal received at the centre, correctly identified to that account, from where the wearer actually spends time, with two-way voice established on equipment that supports it. And what happens on a miss, which is an escalation with a clock attached rather than a note in a log. The programme is written into the service agreement so the wearer knows the contact is coming and can tell a genuine test from a stranger phoning about her alarm. Every result, pass or fail, accumulates into the only account-specific evidence that this service was actually working.

included: interval design justified against the platform's supervision window
the initiation model and the pass criteria including location and voice
the escalation clock on a missed or failed test and the accumulated test record
excluded: the installation-day end-to-end test and first training, which belong to the setup knowledge base
the monitoring centre's internal answering and dispatch procedure, which the operator does not control
any statement about response performance not measured on this account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the platform supervision window, a new device class in the fleet, or a failure that a passing test had not predicted

pros.claim: A tested chain converts a marketing claim into account-specific evidence the operator actually owns
pros.example: a dated log showing this pendant reached the centre from this back bedroom last period, instead of a brochure range figure

pros.claim: Regular practice presses reduce hesitation at the moment it matters
pros.example: a wearer who has pressed the button on a scheduled test being willing to press it on the floor at night rather than waiting to be found

cons.claim: Test contact intrudes on the day of someone who did not want a monitored life in the first place
cons.example: a wearer who stops answering her telephone because the test call feels like being checked up on

cons.claim: A cadence that is easy to run becomes a ritual nobody reads, and misses pile up unnoticed
cons.example: a queue of failed tests logged and never escalated because the log is only opened after something goes wrong

failure_modes: setting the interval from staff convenience rather than from the platform's supervision window
counting a received signal as a pass when voice was never established on equipment that supports it
testing from the hallway next to the base unit rather than from the rooms the wearer actually uses
acceptance_tests: the written cadence names the interval, its relationship to the platform supervision window, the pass criteria and the escalation clock on a miss
each account's test log shows the last result with a date, the location tested from, and the outcome of any escalation
revisit_triggers: the monitoring platform changes its supervision behaviour or reporting
a device class with different supervision characteristics enters the fleet
a missed-signal investigation traces a fault the cadence should have caught earlier

nodes.definition: Read what the equipment and the monitoring platform already report about their own condition, and turn it into a per-account health state instead of leaving it in a feed nobody watches. The signals that exist in this business are specific: low-battery reports from the pendant and from the base unit's backup cell, supervisory check-ins saying a unit is still present and reachable, mains-loss and restore events when a base is unplugged or the neighbourhood power fails, cellular registration and signal-quality indications on mobile units, docking behaviour on rechargeable pendants, and tamper or out-of-range reports. The first job is to establish which of these the operator's specific centre and platform actually deliver and in what form, because it varies by contract and by equipment and is routinely over-assumed. The second is to define what each event obliges: some justify a call the same day, some a scheduled visit, some only a dated note. The third is the honesty rule that binds the whole unit — endurance, range and connectivity are characteristics of this account's equipment in this house, established by these events and the test programme, and are never restated from a datasheet to a worried family.

included: enumerating which supervisory events the operator's own platform actually delivers, confirmed against the monitoring contract
the obligation and response time each event class triggers
the rule that reliability characteristics are verified per account rather than asserted
excluded: device-class selection and honest framing of detection capability at sale, which belong to the setup knowledge base
repairing or modifying equipment outside the manufacturer's procedure
treating device data as information about the person rather than about the equipment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a monitoring contract or platform release note changing the reported event set, or an investigation exposing a fault class the feed never reported

pros.claim: Supervisory events give warning before the wearer notices anything is wrong
pros.example: a mains-loss event followed days later by a low backup-battery report, together identifying a base unplugged when a room was repainted

pros.claim: Grounding every claim in this account's own events keeps the business out of statements it cannot support
pros.example: answering a range question with the account's own test and supervision history rather than a published figure

cons.claim: Telemetry is only as good as the platform's real reporting, which is usually narrower than staff assume
cons.example: discovering that the centre reports low battery but not docking behaviour, leaving rechargeable pendants unmonitored between tests

cons.claim: Event volume without triage becomes noise and trains staff to ignore the feed
cons.example: routine mains-loss events during a neighbourhood outage burying one genuine unit-missing report

failure_modes: assuming a supervisory capability the monitoring contract does not actually provide
reading device events as evidence about the wearer's condition rather than about the equipment
leaving the health feed unwatched between billing cycles
acceptance_tests: the operator holds a written register of the supervisory events their platform delivers, confirmed against the monitoring contract, with the obligation each one triggers
a sampled account's health state is reconstructable from dated platform events rather than from staff recollection
revisit_triggers: the monitoring contract or a platform release changes what is reported
a new device class or transport enters the fleet
an incident investigation finds a fault type the feed never surfaced

nodes.definition: Own the physical consumables that quietly decide whether a device works: pendant cells and rechargeable packs, base-unit backup batteries, neck cords and wrist bands that fray or get thrown away, charging cradles whose contacts stop making, and mounting hardware for wall units. The design question is what triggers a replacement. Calendar-only replacement wastes parts and visits on healthy units; event-only replacement waits for a low-battery report that may arrive after the wearer's next emergency. The workable rule is a triggered routine with several independent triggers — the platform's low-battery report, any real activation that drew heavily on a cell, the manufacturer's stated service life for that specific part, and replacement on sight during any visit for anything visibly worn. Every replacement is recorded against the account with the part and the date, so endurance becomes an observed property of this operator's own fleet rather than a repeated claim. Logistics matter more than they look: a replacement that waits a week on an order is a week of degraded protection, and posting a cell to an older adult who cannot open the housing or does not want to try is not a replacement at all, it is a record of one.

included: the consumable inventory per device class and the independent replacement triggers
the dated per-account replacement record that builds an observed endurance picture
stock holding and delivery reality including who physically performs the change
excluded: device selection, mounting and placement decisions, which belong to the setup knowledge base
repairs using parts the manufacturer does not sanction
asserting any battery endurance figure that this fleet's own record does not support

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed service life in this fleet diverging from the manufacturer's figure, or a supplier discontinuing a part still in use

pros.claim: Multiple independent triggers catch the failure a calendar misses and skip the visit a calendar wastes
pros.example: replacing a pendant cell immediately after a long two-way conversation during a real activation rather than waiting for the next scheduled cycle

pros.claim: Recorded replacements build a real endurance picture for this operator's own mixed fleet
pros.example: noticing that one pendant generation's cells are being replaced far sooner than another's under comparable use

cons.claim: Triggered replacement depends on reports that may never arrive, so it needs the test programme underneath it
cons.example: a pendant whose low-battery report never reached the centre because the unit had already gone silent

cons.claim: Holding stock across several device generations ties up money and shelf space in a small operation
cons.example: keeping cells, cradles and bands for a mixed fleet accumulated across years of installations

failure_modes: posting a part to a wearer who physically cannot fit it and recording the account as remediated
letting a replacement wait on a supplier order while the account stays live and degraded
changing a battery without running a test signal afterwards
acceptance_tests: every replacement is recorded with the part, the date and the trigger that caused it
any replacement touching the alarm path has a post-replacement test result recorded against the account
revisit_triggers: a part's observed service life diverges from the manufacturer's stated figure
a supplier discontinues a cell, cradle or band still in the fleet
an investigation traces a failure to a consumable

nodes.definition: Keep true the two facts an emergency actually turns on: where the wearer physically is, and who can be reached about them. Both decay silently and neither announces its decay. Contacts move, change numbers, give up landlines, separate, fall out, become too frail to help, and die; wearers spend a winter at a daughter's house, move to a different flat in the same complex, acquire a new entry code after the building changes management, or start sleeping downstairs after a hospital stay. The routine that holds these current has three parts. A scheduled confirmation, ideally folded into the same contact that runs the periodic test so an older adult is not telephoned twice about her own alarm. An event-driven confirmation after anything implying change — a real activation, returned post, a declined payment, a contact who did not answer during an incident, a reported move. And a live-verification habit of actually dialling the numbers rather than reading them back, because a number read back confidently is still a number that may ring nowhere. Confirmed values are written to both the local record and the monitoring centre's copy in the same action, and it is the confirmation date, not the value, that makes a field trustworthy.

included: scheduled and event-driven confirmation of address, access details and every contact
live dialling verification rather than read-back
the dual write to the local record and the monitoring centre's copy, with per-field dating
excluded: the initial construction of the contact tree at installation, which is the setup knowledge base's work
deciding who ought to be on the tree, which is the wearer's and the family's decision
retaining contact information beyond what the service needs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an activation where a contact or the access details failed, or a confirmation pass finding widespread staleness in the tree

pros.claim: Dialling rather than reading back finds the dead number before an emergency finds it
pros.example: a scheduled verification reaching a disconnected tone on the first-listed son and prompting a replacement contact that week

pros.claim: Folding confirmation into the test contact avoids repeated nuisance calls to an older adult
pros.example: confirming the address, entry code and top two contacts during the same call that runs the periodic test

cons.claim: Contact churn in an ageing cohort can outrun any reasonable confirmation cadence
cons.example: a first contact who was well at the last confirmation and is himself in hospital on the night of the activation

cons.claim: Repeated verification can feel like surveillance to a family that already resents the arrangement
cons.example: a daughter asking to be taken off the tree because the business contacts her about it more often than her mother does

failure_modes: updating the local record and never the monitoring centre's copy
accepting a relative's second-hand report of a new address without confirming it with the wearer
carrying a contact who has died because nobody wanted to be the one to raise it
acceptance_tests: the account shows a dated confirmation for the service address, the access details and each contact, with the verification method recorded
a sampled change is demonstrably present in both the local record and the monitoring centre's copy
revisit_triggers: an activation in which a listed contact could not be reached
returned post, a declined payment or any reported move
a change of building management, entry code or access arrangement

nodes.definition: Confront the failure mode that no amount of equipment quality repairs: the pendant in the bedside drawer, hanging on the bathroom hook, or still sitting in its cradle while the wearer is out in the garden. Detect it from what is genuinely observable — a rechargeable unit that never leaves the charger, a mobile unit whose location never changes while the household plainly does, wear-detection or activity indications where the equipment provides them, a test call the wearer answers from a room the pendant is not in, and the plainest source of all, the family's own report. Then handle it as a conversation rather than an enforcement action, because the reasons are real and rarely stubbornness: it is uncomfortable, it looks to visitors like an admission, it catches on a cardigan, it went through the wash, or the wearer simply does not want to be the sort of person who wears one. The moves available are practical and come from the fleet — a wrist band instead of a neck cord, a different form factor, a second unit for the bathroom, a placement conversation. The honest last move is to say plainly that a device which is not worn is not protection, and to let the family decide what to do about that, including deciding to stop paying for it.

included: the observable indications of non-wear and their weakness as evidence
the practical remedies available from the operator's own fleet
the plain statement that an unworn device is not protection, and the family's right to act on it
excluded: pressuring, shaming or lecturing a wearer into compliance
any clinical assessment of why the wearer resists wearing it
reporting wear behaviour to anyone the account's disclosure permissions do not cover

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a wear inference proven wrong by the household, or an activation showing the device was not being worn despite passing indications

pros.claim: Naming non-wear early converts a silent false sense of safety into a fixable equipment question
pros.example: swapping a neck cord for a wrist band after a wearer explains the pendant catches on her cardigan

pros.claim: Saying plainly that an unworn device is not protection stops a family paying for reassurance they are not receiving
pros.example: telling a son the account can be ended rather than continuing to bill for a pendant that lives in a drawer

cons.claim: Wear inference from device data is weak evidence and can be wrong in ways that insult the wearer
cons.example: reading a stationary mobile unit as non-wear when the wearer simply had a quiet week indoors with a cold

cons.claim: Raising non-wear can ignite exactly the family conflict the wearer was avoiding
cons.example: a daughter using the business's observation as ammunition in an argument about whether her father should still live alone

failure_modes: treating non-wear as a compliance problem and lecturing the wearer about it
sharing wear observations with a relative the disclosure map does not authorise
continuing to bill a knowingly unworn device because nobody wants to open the conversation
acceptance_tests: an account flagged for non-wear shows the observation, the conversation, the remedy offered and the wearer's own decision
no wear observation appears in a communication to a party outside the account's disclosure permissions
revisit_triggers: a fleet device gains or loses a wear-detection capability
the family reports a change in routine or living arrangement
a real activation reveals the device was not being worn

nodes.definition: Compose the separate streams — last test result, outstanding supervisory events, consumable status, confirmation dates on address and contacts, non-wear indications, recent activations and any open service item — into one dated health state per account, and convert the unhealthy ones into a worked queue with owners. Without this step each stream is watched by whoever happens to look at it and nobody owns the account as a whole. The composition rule is deliberately blunt: an account is healthy only when every component is current and passing, so a perfect device sitting behind a two-year-old contact confirmation is not a healthy account. The queue is ordered by exposure rather than by convenience — a failed test with an unreachable first contact outranks a frayed lanyard — and every item carries an owner and a due date, because a list of known problems without owners is just a record of what the business already knew when something went wrong. The review is also the only place where cross-account patterns become visible: a device generation failing tests more often than its peers, or a whole building losing a signal path after a wiring change, both of which belong to the fleet-level work rather than to twenty separate accounts.

included: the composition rule turning component streams into one dated state
exposure-ordered triage with an owner and a due date per item
escalation of cross-account patterns to the fleet-level work
excluded: the individual monitoring routines themselves, which are their own work units
commercial account management such as upgrade or upsell activity
any judgment about the wearer's health, capability or living situation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an incident on an account the review had marked healthy, or a book size that the current cadence demonstrably cannot cover

pros.claim: One composed state makes the question of whether an account is actually protected right now answerable in a sentence
pros.example: answering a daughter's question about her mother's service with a dated health state rather than three separate system lookups

pros.claim: Exposure ordering sends the scarce visit to the account carrying the real risk
pros.example: routing the week's single field visit to a failed test with an unreachable contact rather than to a cosmetic complaint

cons.claim: A strict all-components rule leaves a long amber list that can demoralise a small team
cons.example: most of the book showing unhealthy purely on contact-confirmation age after a quarter dominated by installations

cons.claim: Composition can hide the specific fact that mattered behind a single status word
cons.example: an account marked healthy overall while the note that its backup battery is ageing goes unread

failure_modes: reviewing only the accounts that have already complained
letting the queue exist without owners or due dates so it becomes a list of known problems
scoring health from device data alone and ignoring contact and address staleness
acceptance_tests: every live account carries a dated health state derived from the named component streams
each unhealthy account has an owner, a due date and a recorded outcome
revisit_triggers: a pattern appears across multiple accounts on one device generation or one building
the composition rule is shown by a real incident to have mis-ranked exposure
the book grows past what the current review cadence can actually cover

nodes.definition: Decide in advance what the business proactively tells the family, through which channel and how quickly, so that communication is a designed part of the service rather than whatever the person who happened to answer the telephone decided. The events that plainly warrant a proactive contact are a real activation, a failed test not resolved on the spot, a device fault leaving the account unprotected, a supervisory report suggesting a unit is missing or unpowered, and a change one party made that the wearer has not confirmed. The events that do not warrant one are routine passes, ordinary consumable replacements and anything merely interesting. Channel matters because the audience is split three ways: the wearer usually wants a voice on the telephone, the adult child usually wants something written they can read between meetings, and a professional caregiver usually wants the shortest true fact and nothing else. Content is bounded absolutely by the account's disclosure permissions, and register matters as much as content — report the event and the equipment, do not narrate the wearer's body, and never let a service update carry an offer, because a family that learns updates come attached to selling stops reading them.

included: the proactive-contact event list with audience, channel and target timeframe
content bounded by the disclosure permissions and the register rules
the prohibition on attaching any offer to a service communication
excluded: pre-sale communication with the family, which belongs to the acquisition knowledge base
clinical explanation of what happened to the wearer during an event
contact with any party the disclosure map excludes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a family reporting they were not told about a qualifying event, or a disclosure permission change that alters who may receive updates

pros.claim: A defined proactive list ends the pattern where families only hear from the business when something is being sold
pros.example: a written note after a failed test explaining what was found and when the visit is, sent before the daughter has to ask

pros.claim: Matching the channel to the audience raises the chance the message is actually received
pros.example: a voice call to the wearer and a short written summary to the son who cannot take calls at work

cons.claim: Proactive contact after every qualifying event costs hours a small operation must fund from somewhere
cons.example: an activation-heavy week in which follow-up calls displace scheduled maintenance visits

cons.claim: Written updates create a permanent record that can be read uncharitably long afterwards
cons.example: an early note describing a suspected fault being quoted back during a complaint after the investigation found a different cause

failure_modes: letting whoever answers the telephone decide what may be disclosed
sending updates to the payer that the wearer never authorised
attaching an upgrade offer to a service update
acceptance_tests: each qualifying event type has a stated audience, channel and target timeframe
a sampled activation shows a recorded contact consistent with that account's disclosure permissions
revisit_triggers: the disclosure permissions on an account change
a family reports learning about an event from someone other than the business
the operator adds a channel such as messaging or a family portal

nodes.definition: Hold, for the whole life of the subscription, that the person wearing the device is the customer, even when somebody else pays for it. This is a set of enforced rules and not a sentiment. The wearer decides what is disclosed and to whom. The wearer may decline a remedy, a form factor, a visit or an upgrade. The wearer may cancel, and that instruction is executed rather than routed to the payer for approval. The wearer is addressed directly and first in every contact and is not discussed in the third person while sitting in the room. The language used about them describes events and equipment rather than decline. And no observation the business makes about their behaviour is ever used to move them toward a decision about how or where they live. The counter-pressure is constant and comes from good people: a frightened adult child, a caregiver who wants oversight, a business that would prefer to keep the revenue. The enforcement mechanisms are small and concrete — an opening script that speaks to the wearer, a disclosure check before any family contact, a rule that the wearer's own cancellation is actioned on the call — and they only survive if they are written into the workflow rather than into a values statement.

included: the enumerated autonomy rules and the workflow mechanism that enforces each
the practice of addressing the wearer first and directly
the ban on using service observations to steer the wearer's life decisions
excluded: determining capacity or competence, which this business never judges
adjudicating disputes between family members
the pre-sale vulnerable-consumer rules, which belong to the acquisition knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint or family dispute revealing an autonomy rule that was bypassed, or a wearer restating their preferences

pros.claim: Treating the wearer as the customer keeps the device something she owns rather than something done to her, which is what makes it worn at all
pros.example: a wearer who chose her own wrist form factor continuing to wear it after refusing the pendant her son had picked

pros.claim: A clear rule about whose instruction is executed ends an argument the business would otherwise lose slowly and expensively
pros.example: cancelling on the wearer's own instruction without first telephoning the daughter who pays for it

cons.claim: Honouring the wearer's choice can leave the family and the business watching a risk that neither may act on
cons.example: a wearer who declines to allow any disclosure of an activation to her children

cons.claim: The paying relative may end the account when their preferences are not the ones honoured
cons.example: a payer who cancels after being told he cannot receive the wear reports his mother declined to authorise

failure_modes: letting the payer become the decision-maker because they answer the telephone and the wearer does not
using pity or fear language about the wearer in conversations with the family
routing the wearer's own cancellation through the person who pays
acceptance_tests: each autonomy rule names the specific workflow mechanism that enforces it
a sampled family contact shows the disclosure check was performed before any information was given
revisit_triggers: a family dispute reaches the business
a wearer changes their disclosure or authority preferences
a new member of staff joins the service side

nodes.definition: Define how the business interacts with the other people around the wearer — home-care aides, building managers and front desks, adult day programmes, neighbours and church networks, and facility staff after a move — without drifting into pretending to coordinate care. The useful interactions are narrow and mechanical. Make sure an aide knows what the device does and does not do, and how to avoid triggering it during transfers and bathing. Make sure a building's desk knows there is a monitored unit in a particular flat and how access will be needed if responders arrive. Make sure any professional listed on the contact tree knows they are listed, what being listed obliges, and has consented to it. Make sure a residence that already runs its own call system knows a personal device is present so the two arrangements do not quietly cancel each other out in the family's understanding. The boundary is the charter's: this business relays signals and maintains equipment. It does not take instructions about the wearer's care, does not accept clinical information it has no basis to act on, and does not become the channel through which a professional passes something that belongs with the family or a clinician.

included: the narrow mechanical briefings for aides, building desks and facility staff
recorded consent from any professional listed on the contact tree
the non-coordination boundary and how it is stated to the other party
excluded: care coordination, case management or clinical communication of any kind
professional referral-channel development for acquisition, which belongs to the acquisition knowledge base
any compensation arrangement with a professional, which sits inside that knowledge base's inducement boundary

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a care arrangement change around the wearer, or an incident in which another party acted on an assumption about what the service does

pros.claim: Briefing an aide removes a large share of avoidable nuisance activations and missed presses at once
pros.example: an aide who now unclips the pendant before a shower transfer and clips it back afterwards instead of triggering it or leaving it off the wearer

pros.claim: Telling a building desk in advance prevents responders being held at a locked lobby
pros.example: a concierge who knows which flat holds a monitored unit and has the access instruction already on file

cons.claim: Every additional party raises the chance information reaches someone the wearer never authorised
cons.example: a building manager who starts relaying alarm gossip to neighbours in the lift

cons.claim: Professionals can read a helpful interface as an invitation to hand over responsibility
cons.example: an aide who assumes the monitoring service will notice that her client did not answer the door this morning

failure_modes: accepting clinical instructions the business is neither qualified nor contracted to act on
listing a professional on the contact tree without their knowledge or consent
letting a residence assume the personal device is part of its own nurse-call arrangement
acceptance_tests: every professional listed as a contact has a recorded consent and knows what being listed obliges
each interface type has a written boundary statement staff can read aloud to the other party
revisit_triggers: the wearer moves into a building or residence with its own call system
the aide or the home-care agency changes
a nuisance-activation pattern traces to handling during care tasks

nodes.definition: Treat every real activation as an event that leaves the account degraded until it is deliberately restored, rather than as an incident that ended when the ambulance pulled away. The routine has a fixed shape. Restore the equipment: the pendant cell that carried a long two-way conversation, the base unit that may have been unplugged or moved during the response, the unit that went to hospital in a coat pocket. Prove the chain again with a test signal, because the account has just demonstrated it matters. Re-confirm the facts the event exercised — which contacts actually answered, whether the access details worked, whether responders reached the door without delay — since an activation supplies verification no scheduled routine can produce. Contact the wearer in the register of a check-in rather than an interview, and contact the family strictly inside the disclosure permissions. Retrieve the monitoring centre's own account of the event promptly, while it is still retrievable, and attach it to the record. Then read what the event revealed about the account, because activations are the single richest source of truth about whether this arrangement actually works in this house.

included: equipment restoration and the mandatory post-event test
verification of contacts and access details from what the event exposed
the wearer check-in, the bounded family contact and prompt retrieval of the centre's event record
excluded: any clinical follow-up or advice about the wearer's condition or recovery
investigation of a failed activation, which is its own work unit
using the check-in as an occasion to sell an upgrade or ask for a referral

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the centre's record retention, or aftercare findings showing a recurring contact or access failure across accounts

pros.claim: Immediate restoration closes the window in which an account sits silently unprotected right after its most dangerous day
pros.example: replacing a heavily used pendant cell and re-testing the morning after an overnight activation

pros.claim: The event supplies verification of the contact tree and access details that no scheduled confirmation could match
pros.example: learning that the second contact answered while the first did not, and reordering the tree that week

cons.claim: Aftercare lands exactly when the family has least attention to spare for the business
cons.example: a check-in call reaching a daughter standing in a hospital corridor

cons.claim: Monitoring-centre event records may be limited or short-lived, so late retrieval loses the account of what happened
cons.example: requesting a call record after the centre's retention window and receiving only a one-line summary

failure_modes: closing the activation when the response ended and never restoring the equipment
waiting for the family to report what the event revealed instead of asking
turning the check-in into an upgrade conversation
acceptance_tests: every activation has a completed aftercare record showing equipment restored, a post-event test result and the contact and access observations
the monitoring centre's event record is requested within its stated retention window and attached to the account
revisit_triggers: the centre changes its event-record retention or format
aftercare reviews show a recurring gap such as a contact who never answers
activation volume outgrows the routine's capacity

nodes.definition: When a family says they pressed and no help came, reconstruct what actually happened along the whole chain before saying anything about cause, and move fast enough that the evidence still exists. The chain has known failure points and each carries its own evidence. The button and its cell, whose state can be read and bench-tested. The radio or cellular path from where the wearer actually was, which must be re-tested from that exact spot rather than from the hallway. The base unit's power and connectivity, whose mains-loss and supervision history the platform holds. The monitoring centre's own record of what it received, when, and what it did, which must be requested formally and immediately because retention is the centre's policy and not the operator's. The contact tree, where the failure is very often that the right people were called and did not answer. The access details, where responders arrived and could not get in. And the human layer, where the press happened somewhere the device was not, or did not happen at all. The output is a dated reconstruction that separates what is established from what is inferred from what cannot be determined, and it is written before anyone from the business offers the family an explanation.

included: the enumerated failure points and the evidence source for each
a formal and immediate request for the monitoring centre's own record
the established / inferred / undetermined structure of the written reconstruction
excluded: assigning legal liability or making admissions on any party's behalf, which is counsel's work
clinical judgment about the outcome for the wearer
the customer-facing disclosure itself, which is the service-recovery work unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a repeat failure of the same class, or a change in what the monitoring centre will retain and disclose

pros.claim: Reconstructing before explaining stops the business asserting a cause that later proves wrong in front of the same family
pros.example: an early theory of a flat battery giving way to a base unit unplugged for a week, once the mains-loss history was actually read

pros.claim: Re-testing from the exact spot the wearer was in produces evidence a hallway test would never generate
pros.example: reproducing a failed press at the far end of a detached garage rather than beside the base unit in the kitchen

cons.claim: Evidence decays quickly and much of it lives with a third party the operator does not control
cons.example: a monitoring centre whose call audio is retained only briefly and must be requested within days

cons.claim: A careful investigation reads as stalling to a family that wants an answer tonight
cons.example: a son escalating publicly while the reconstruction is still open and honestly incomplete

failure_modes: accepting the monitoring centre's summary without requesting the underlying record
closing the investigation at the first plausible cause that fits
letting a staff member offer the family a theory during the very first call
acceptance_tests: the reconstruction covers every named failure point with its evidence, or an explicit note that it could not be determined
the request to the monitoring centre is dated inside the retention window and its response is attached to the account
revisit_triggers: a second failure of the same class occurs anywhere in the book
the monitoring centre changes its record-retention or disclosure practice
a test that passed shortly before the failure suggests the cadence or the pass criteria are too weak

nodes.definition: Tell the family what the reconstruction found, in plain language, including the parts that are the business's own fault and the parts that cannot be determined, and then fix what can actually be fixed. The disclosure has a shape: what was established, what the business got wrong, what has already been changed on this account, what still cannot be promised even now, and what the family's options are including leaving. The remedy is designed from the established cause rather than from goodwill — a replaced or different-class device where the equipment failed, a rebuilt contact tree where the tree failed, a changed access instruction where responders were delayed, a credit or refund where the service was simply not delivered. No remedy is ever conditioned on the family staying subscribed, withholding a complaint, or signing anything that trades silence for money. Escalation and reporting duties, including whether an incident class must be reported to the monitoring partner, an equipment maker or a regulator, are an obligation class the operator verifies currently in their own jurisdiction. What earns a relationship back, when anything does, is that the family was told something true they could not have obtained any other way.

included: the five-part disclosure structure including remaining uncertainty and the option to leave
remedy designed from the established cause
the rule that no remedy is conditioned on silence or continued subscription, and the reporting obligation class
excluded: legal admissions, settlement drafting or insurance strategy, which belong to counsel and the insurer
any clinical statement about the wearer's outcome
retention persuasion dressed up as service recovery

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the incident-reporting obligation class, or a recurrence showing the remedy addressed a symptom rather than the cause

pros.claim: Disclosure the family could not have obtained elsewhere is the only thing that rebuilds trust after a failure
pros.example: showing a daughter the platform's own power-loss history that explains the silent night, including the part the business should have caught weeks earlier

pros.claim: A remedy tied to the established cause repairs the account instead of buying a mood
pros.example: rebuilding the contact tree where the failure was that nobody answered, rather than offering a free month

cons.claim: Candour about fault has consequences the operator carries alone
cons.example: a written acknowledgement that a supervisory report went unread being available to anyone the family later shows it to

cons.claim: Families sometimes want a certainty the evidence cannot support
cons.example: a family asking to be told definitively that the device worked when the only honest answer is that it cannot be determined

failure_modes: offering a credit before the cause is established, which reads as buying off the complaint
conditioning any remedy on staying subscribed or staying quiet
issuing a drafted non-answer where a plain account of what happened was available
acceptance_tests: the disclosure states the established cause, the business's own fault, the changes made, the remaining uncertainty and the family's options including cancellation
no remedy in the record is conditioned on continued subscription or on withholding a complaint
revisit_triggers: counsel or the monitoring partner changes the incident-reporting obligation
a disclosed incident recurs on the same account or the same device class
the same remedy is being applied repeatedly across different accounts

nodes.definition: Handle accidental and repeated activations as a tuning problem with a hard floor underneath it, because the cheapest fix — making the device less likely to fire — is precisely the one that quietly removes the protection the family is paying for. The sources are identifiable: a pendant pressed by a chair arm or a mattress, handling during care transfers and bathing, a detection-class feature reacting to a sharp sit-down or to a dropped pendant, a wearer testing the button because nobody explained how, a visiting grandchild, and equipment faults producing spurious events. The moves that reduce nuisance without reducing coverage are physical and procedural first: cord length and placement, a change of form factor, a guard or cover where the maker supplies one, briefing aides and family, and teaching the wearer to cancel a false activation with the operator rather than by hiding the device. Reducing the sensitivity of a detection feature is a last resort, explained honestly to the family as a trade, and recorded as their decision rather than the operator's convenience. Public-safety false-alarm ordinances and any fee or escalation regime attached to them are an obligation class to verify currently in the operator's jurisdiction.

included: source identification for recurring nuisance activations
the ordered remedy ladder from physical to procedural to sensitivity
the recorded family decision on any sensitivity trade and the local ordinance obligation class
excluded: initial device-class selection and honest framing of detection capability at sale, which belong to the setup knowledge base
disabling protection to reduce the operator's own workload
any promise about detection performance not verified on this account's own equipment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a missed real event on an account with reduced sensitivity, or a nuisance pattern clustering on one device class

pros.claim: Physical and procedural fixes resolve most nuisance activations without touching coverage at all
pros.example: a shorter cord plus a briefing for the morning aide after repeated presses during transfers

pros.claim: Recording a sensitivity trade as the family's informed decision keeps the choice with the people it affects
pros.example: a dated note that detection sensitivity was reduced at the family's request after repeated nuisance events, with the consequence written out

cons.claim: Repeated false alarms erode responder and family trust faster than any tuning can restore it
cons.example: a household that starts telephoning the centre to cancel before checking whether the wearer actually needs help

cons.claim: Some nuisance sources cannot be removed without removing the feature the family bought
cons.example: a wearer whose daily routine reliably produces detection events that are not falls

failure_modes: quietly reducing sensitivity to stop the calls and never telling the family
blaming the wearer for pressing rather than examining placement and handling
ignoring the local false-alarm ordinance class until a fee or a warning notice arrives
acceptance_tests: each recurring nuisance account has a recorded source analysis and remedies applied in order from physical to procedural to sensitivity
any sensitivity change carries the family's recorded decision and the written statement of the trade
revisit_triggers: a device class shows a nuisance pattern across several accounts
the local false-alarm ordinance or fee regime changes
a real event is missed on an account where sensitivity had been reduced

nodes.definition: Plan for the recurring shock in this business: the transport a device depends on is retired, or the monitoring platform changes, and part of a live book quietly loses the ability to signal at all. It has happened with cellular generation shutdowns that stranded mobile units, with fixed-line and copper changes, and with households moving to voice services that do not reliably carry an alarm unit's signalling, and it will happen again. The work has five parts. Know which accounts sit on which transport and which device generation, which requires the account record to actually carry those fields before the announcement rather than after. Get advance notice from the equipment maker, the carrier and the monitoring centre rather than from a wave of failing tests. Sequence the migration by exposure rather than alphabetically, so the most isolated wearers move first. Decide and state the cost position for a forced replacement once, as a commercial position applied to everyone, rather than improvising per family under pressure. And treat every migration as a new installation for the purpose of proving the chain, because a swapped device is an untested device until an end-to-end test says otherwise.

included: transport and device-generation inventory across the whole book
advance-notice sourcing from maker, carrier and monitoring centre
exposure-ordered sequencing, the single stated cost position, and the mandatory post-swap end-to-end test
excluded: device-class selection criteria and installation procedure, which belong to the setup knowledge base
negotiating supplier or carrier contracts
asserting a future shutdown date not confirmed with the carrier or the maker

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a retirement announcement from a carrier, maker or centre, or a cluster of test failures on one transport

pros.claim: An inventory by transport turns a sudden shutdown into a schedulable programme
pros.example: listing every mobile unit on a retiring cellular generation well before the date and sequencing visits from it

pros.claim: Deciding the cost position once prevents a scramble in which the loudest family gets the best terms
pros.example: a stated rule that a forced transport migration is at the operator's cost, applied identically to every affected account

cons.claim: Migration consumes exactly the capacity routine maintenance needs, so the routine work degrades while it runs
cons.example: contact confirmations slipping across the whole book during a fleet swap

cons.claim: Forced replacement is an unwelcome disruption for a wearer who had finally grown used to a device
cons.example: an older adult who must learn a different button and a new charging habit she never asked for

failure_modes: discovering a transport dependency only when tests start failing across a group of accounts
migrating in convenience order rather than in exposure order
treating a device swap as complete without an end-to-end test
acceptance_tests: the book can be listed by transport and device generation with a count per class
every migrated account carries a post-swap end-to-end test result
revisit_triggers: a carrier, equipment maker or monitoring centre announces a retirement or platform change
a household changes its telephone or internet service
test failures cluster on one transport or one device generation

nodes.definition: Classify why accounts end, because the reasons are not variations of a single thing and each demands a different response. The classes that actually occur in this business are: the wearer has died; the wearer has moved to assisted living, a nursing home or a relative's household where other arrangements exist; the wearer is in hospital or rehabilitation and the account's future is genuinely uncertain; the family decided the cost is not justified; the device was never worn; the service failed and trust is gone; a competitor was chosen; and the account was sold to somebody who never wanted it in the first place. Only some of these are addressable by the business at all, and treating the unaddressable ones as retention opportunities is the single most damaging thing a medical-alert operator can do to its own reputation. The taxonomy's real job is routing: bereavement to a dignified stop with no save attempt, higher-care moves to an honest conversation about redundancy, non-wear and service failure to the work units that can actually repair something, and cost or competitor decisions to a plain restatement of terms and an easy exit. It is also the input that makes the recurring book readable rather than merely countable.

included: the enumerated ending classes and the routing of each to its handling path
the rule that unaddressable classes are never treated as save opportunities
the reason mix as the input that makes book health interpretable
excluded: retention campaigns, save-desk scripting and win-back offers of any kind
any inference about the wearer's health or prognosis from the ending class
portfolio economics itself, which is the book-health work unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an ending that does not fit the enumerated classes, or a discovered service failure behind an account closed under another class

pros.claim: Routing by cause stops a bereavement call being answered with a retention script
pros.example: a class that automatically suppresses every save attempt and opens the dignified-stop path instead

pros.claim: A truthful reason mix tells the operator which problems are actually theirs to fix
pros.example: seeing that non-wear and service failure together outweigh cost decisions, and re-aiming the quarter's effort at the health review

cons.claim: The reason given on the telephone is often the polite version rather than the real one
cons.example: a family citing cost when the real reason is a failed activation they never complained about

cons.claim: Classification tempts an operator to treat the addressable classes as targets and push too hard on them
cons.example: an account marked as a cost decision receiving three follow-up calls the family experienced as pressure

failure_modes: collapsing every ending into a single cancelled status
recording the first reason offered without the follow-up question that finds the real one
building a save-desk script from the taxonomy for classes that should never be saved
acceptance_tests: every closed account carries a class from the enumerated list with the date and who reported it
classes marked unaddressable have no save contact recorded against them
revisit_triggers: an ending appears that the taxonomy does not cover
the reason mix shifts materially across a period
a service failure is later discovered behind an account closed under a different class

nodes.definition: Handle the most common living-arrangement ending honestly, which in this business usually means telling a family they may not need the subscription any more. When a wearer moves into assisted living, a nursing home or a care-equipped household, the questions are concrete. Does the destination already run its own call system, and does it cover the wearer's room, the bathroom and the common areas, or does it stop at doors the wearer will still walk through alone. Will the wearer keep a mobile unit for outings, which is a genuine remaining use that a building's fixed system does not cover. Is the household destination one where a personal device still helps, or one where somebody is always present. And does the family want a suspension rather than a cancellation because a rehabilitation stay may end with a return home. The business's obligations are to say plainly where the service is likely redundant before the family asks, to offer suspension only where it genuinely serves the customer rather than as a way to avoid recording a cancellation, to transfer a subscription to another household member only where that person actually wants it and is enrolled properly from the start, and to make the equipment return simple whichever way the decision goes.

included: the redundancy assessment against the destination's own arrangements including coverage gaps
suspension used only where it serves the customer, with an end date and an owner
transfer to another wearer treated as a fresh enrolment, and simple equipment return
excluded: advising on facility choice, care level or whether a move is appropriate, which are family and clinical decisions
negotiating with a facility on the family's behalf
using suspension as a retention tactic

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a suspension that outlived its purpose, or a residence coverage description found to be wrong in practice

pros.claim: Volunteering that the service may be redundant is the clearest demonstration of honesty this business can make, and families remember it
pros.example: telling a daughter that her mother's new residence covers the room and cancelling, then receiving her neighbour's enquiry months later

pros.claim: Distinguishing indoor coverage from outings finds the genuine remaining use instead of inventing one
pros.example: keeping a mobile unit for a wearer who still walks to the shops from a residence whose system stops at the front door

cons.claim: Honest redundancy advice ends revenue a less scrupulous competitor would have kept
cons.example: a book that loses accounts on transitions another operator would simply have let run

cons.claim: Suspension can quietly become an account that pays nothing and consumes service attention indefinitely
cons.example: a rehabilitation suspension nobody revisits for many months while the equipment sits in a family's cupboard

failure_modes: letting a family assume the device still works as before in a residence with its own system and different coverage
offering suspension mainly to avoid recording a cancellation
transferring an account to a relative who never assented to wearing anything
acceptance_tests: a transition record states whether the destination's arrangements make the service redundant and what the family decided
every suspension carries an end date and a named owner who revisits it
revisit_triggers: a suspension passes its review date
a residence relationship reveals a coverage gap the business had described wrongly
the wearer returns home

nodes.definition: Have one path ready for the call that says the wearer has died, and make it the shortest and gentlest process in the business. Billing stops on notification, not on paperwork, and the stop is confirmed in writing to whoever called. No save attempt of any kind is made, no reason is probed beyond what the caller volunteers, and no offer is ever attached to a condolence. Any prepaid period beyond the stop is refunded on the operator's own stated rule rather than negotiated by a grieving relative in the moment, with automatic-renewal and refund duties treated as an obligation class to verify currently in the operator's jurisdiction. Equipment return is made easy and unhurried: a prepaid mailer, collection during a later visit to the area, or a written waiver where retrieval would be an intrusion, and never a debt-collection posture over a pendant. The account is closed with its class recorded so the book stays truthful, and the household is suppressed from every marketing and referral list immediately so that no promotion ever arrives after a funeral. If that family later returns for another relative, they return to a business that treated them well at the worst possible moment.

included: immediate billing stop on notification with written confirmation
refund of any prepaid period on the operator's own stated rule, as an obligation class to verify
unhurried equipment return options and immediate marketing and referral suppression
excluded: probate, estate or legal advice about the deceased's affairs
requiring documentary proof before stopping the billing
any retention, win-back or referral approach to a bereaved household

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint about billing or contact after a death, or a change in the jurisdiction's refund and renewal obligation class

pros.claim: Stopping billing on the caller's word costs little and prevents the single worst reputational event this business can produce
pros.example: a charge appearing on a deceased mother's account weeks after the family telephoned, which is the story that gets repeated at every family gathering

pros.claim: A prepared path spares staff from improvising during a call most people find hard
pros.example: a written sequence a new employee can follow when a son calls at the end of a very long week

cons.claim: Acting on an unverified notification risks stopping service for somebody who is alive
cons.example: a confused or malicious call reporting a death that did not occur

cons.claim: Waiving equipment retrieval writes off assets a small operator has already paid for
cons.example: several units written off across a year of bereavement closures

failure_modes: requiring a death certificate before stopping the billing
sending an equipment-return demand to a grieving household
leaving the household on a marketing list so a promotion arrives after the funeral
acceptance_tests: the billing stop is dated to the notification rather than to any document, and a written confirmation is on file
the household is suppressed from all marketing and referral contact at closure
revisit_triggers: the operator's refund or automatic-renewal obligation class changes in the jurisdiction
an equipment-return approach causes distress or a complaint
a notification is later found to have been mistaken

nodes.definition: Build an exit at least as easy as the entry, and be able to prove it rather than assert it. The mechanics that matter are specific. Who may cancel: the wearer always, plus anyone the authority map lists, and the wearer's own instruction is never routed to the payer for approval. How: at minimum the same channels that could be used to sign up, not a single telephone line during weekday hours. When it takes effect and how the final bill is computed, under the operator's own stated rule rather than a negotiation. How the recurring payment authorisation is actually stopped, which is the step that produces the worst complaints in this industry when a service record is closed and a payment instruction is not. How equipment comes back, with a prepaid method and a stated grace period. And the written confirmation the customer receives without having to ask for it. Automatic-renewal, negative-option and cancellation-channel duties differ by jurisdiction and change, and are an obligation class the operator verifies currently in their own. The provable part is a symmetry test: count the steps, channels and elapsed time to join, count them to leave, and any excess is the retention gauntlet the business claims not to run.

included: the who, how, when, final-bill, payment-stop, equipment-return and confirmation mechanics
the symmetry test against the sign-up path
the renewal and cancellation-channel obligation class flagged for jurisdictional verification
excluded: contract term design and disclosure at the point of sale, which belong to the acquisition knowledge base
collections and debt-recovery strategy
save offers and retention scripting of any kind

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a billing-after-cancellation complaint, a new sign-up channel, or a jurisdictional change in cancellation-channel obligations

pros.claim: A symmetry test turns an easy-cancellation promise into something auditable rather than asserted
pros.example: finding that joining takes one call while leaving requires a posted letter, and closing the gap the same week
